What population state is dynamically stable?
Converges to ε-Nash in zero-sum EFG
Gradient flow on the simplex: ẋᵢ = xᵢ(fᵢ(x) − f̄(x)) is proportional to the gradient of average fitness; for potential games this is gradient ascent on the potential function
Lyapunov stability in dynamical systems: the ESS condition (f(y,x*) < f(x*,x*) for y ≠ x*) is exactly the condition that x* is a strict local minimum of the Lyapunov function
Load balancing across servers: each request routed to minimize personal latency, ignoring the load it adds to others — distributed routing under selfish scheduling
Counterintuitive in distributed systems: adding a faster node or link can increase overall latency if it concentrates load — relevant to CDN routing, load balancer configurations
Distributed system efficiency ratio: the worst-case overhead from removing central coordination; PoA ≤ 4/3 for linear latency = selfish routing degrades performance by at most 33% vs. optimal routing

The game has an exact potential Φ: each unilateral improvement step increases Φ, so best-response dynamics terminates (finite improvement property) — same as finding a descent direction in convex optimization

Online learning / online convex optimization: each round choose a distribution over actions, receive loss, update via multiplicative weights — MIT OCW: Lecture on Online Learning covers the full theory

Convergence of decentralized learning: if all players run no-regret algorithms, the empirical joint distribution converges to the set of correlated equilibria — distributed coordination without communication
Deep RL / game solving: basis for AlphaHoldem, Libratus, Pluribus (superhuman poker); converges to Nash in two-player zero-sum EFGs by minimizing local regrets at each information set
